summary: Humanity's leap from tool-using apes to a voyage beyond Jupiter, where the computer HAL turns killer and Bowman passes through the Star Gate to be reborn.

hunger.why: The starving apes scavenge until the bone tool lets them eat meat, and the astronauts eat paste from trays.

thirst.why: The rival ape tribes fight over the waterhole in the opening section.

feeling-cold-hot.why: Bowman is exposed to the vacuum of space without a helmet, a brief ordeal.

sleepiness.why: Three crew members lie in hibernation until HAL cuts their life support, and Floyd sleeps on the shuttle.

curiosity.why: The apes touch the monolith, Floyd's team visits the Tycho excavation, Discovery flies to Jupiter, and Bowman enters the Star Gate; the unknown pulls every section forward.

explanation-seeking.why: What the monolith is and why it signals Jupiter is the mission's question, and the crew must work out whether HAL has failed.

skill-acquisition.why: The ape learns to wield a bone as a weapon, humanity's first tool.

resource-foraging.why: The apes forage for food and water in the desert.

mental-time-travel.why: Bowman and Poole plan how to handle HAL, and the mission's secret purpose is planned on Earth.

fear-of-predators.why: A leopard kills an ape in the opening, and the apes huddle at night listening to it.

fear-of-aggressors.why: The rival apes attack at the waterhole, and HAL kills Poole and the sleeping crew and locks Bowman out of the ship.

fear-of-heights.why: Poole's body tumbles into space and the pod scenes play on weightless drops, faintly.

pain-aversion.why: Poole's air line is cut and Bowman risks decompression, but suffering is barely shown.

pride.why: The ape brandishes the bone in triumph, and the Tycho scientists are congratulated.

moral-pride.why: No one upholds values at cost.

guilt.why: No one feels guilt, though HAL pleads as he is shut down.

warmth.why: Floyd's video call with his small daughter is a brief tender moment.

moral-blame.why: HAL's murders are not condemned so much as survived.

moral-praise.why: No one is celebrated for goodness.

revenge.why: Bowman disconnects HAL to survive, not to punish.

compassion.why: Bowman tries to retrieve Poole's body, and HAL's pleading stirs a flicker of pity.

friendship.why: Bowman and Poole are quiet crewmates who confide in the pod.

sadness.why: HAL's fading voice singing Daisy is the film's one moment of loss.

humor.why: The zero-gravity toilet instructions are a dry joke.

reasoning.why: Bowman and Poole argue over HAL's reliability inside the pod.

coalitional-affiliation.why: The ape tribes confront each other as groups at the waterhole.

status-seeking.why: The armed ape tribe claims dominance of the waterhole.

anger.why: The ape's frenzy with the bone is the film's one burst of rage.

parental-care.why: Floyd calls his daughter about her birthday, and the Star Child closes the film as a newborn.

familial-love.why: Poole watches a birthday message from his parents, a brief family tie.
